Aprilia Obscure Spe.Ed. Is an Even Lighter RSV4 with Leg Wings, Just 500 to Be Made
9 photos
Photo: autoevolution/Cristian Curmei
Italian bike maker Aprilia is one of the most unforgiving forces in two-wheeled motorsport. The company has no less than 54 titles to its name in various competitions, so when it announces a new version of a bike that was responsible for seven of those titles in the World Superbike Championship, the world is bound to pay attention.
That bike would be the mighty RSV4 , a platform that has been periodically honored with more and more extreme versions of itself. Taking advantage of the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA) show in Milan, Italy, which opens its doors this week, a new such version, perhaps the most extreme one yet, comes under the spotlight.
They call it the RSV4 Obscure Spe.Ed., and it is supposed to be a limited-edition version (only 500, each of them numbered, are being planned) designed specifically, but not exclusively, for the racetrack.
The main focus of the Italian engineers fell on making the motorcycle as light as possible. Since there weren't all that many things that could be removed to cut weight, Aprilia went for carbon fiber parts wherever possible, including the mudguards, side panels, footrest guards, and front brake air intakes.
The bike shed the most pounds off its wheels, with the new carbon ones being 4.4 pounds (two kg) lighter than the wheels fitted on the RSV4 Factory. In all, the total weight of the Obscure Spe.Ed. Is 6.6 pounds (three kg) less than the Factory version.
That would be a total of 432 pounds (196 kg) for the newcomer, when the ART (Aprilia Racing Technology) exhaust system is fitted. Without it, the motorcycle tips the scales at 443 pounds (201 kg).
But cutting weight is not the only way one can make a bike faster and more effective on the track. Aerodynamic elements matter, too, and it is here that Aprilia likes to play the toughest game.
For the new version of the RSV4, Aprilia imagined something called leg wings, carbon fiber extra fittings designed to increase downforce by up to 20 percent. Already previewed on the RS-GP prototype, the solution makes its debut on a production limited edition superbike.
The heart of the two-wheeled monster continues to be the same engine that powers the RSV4 and RSV4 Factory, a narrow-V four-cylinder powerplant the bike maker likes to call a world first.
As the company's most powerful engine ever, the 1,099cc piece of tech is rated at 220 hp at 13,000 rpm and 127 Nm of torque at 10,800 rpm. When riders opt for the ART exhaust system, those numbers jump to 223 hp and almost 132 Nm of torque.
The suspension system on the Obscure Spe.Ed. Is new as well, and it consists of an Ohlins NIX fork at the front and an Ohlins TTX shock at the rear. These elements tie into wheels measuring 17 inches on both ends.
Aprilia says it will offer the RSV4 Obscure Spe.Ed. (that funky word is supposed to be a contraction of Special Edition) in a single color, black all over, but makes no mention of how much it will charge for one of these babies. Knowing this company, though, it will probably not be cheap.
Especially if you take into account that this new version has now become the new flagship of the RSV4 range.
